setup.agents.saveUserBody: It's written to {{file}}, outside this workspace, so History can't roll it back. You can still edit or delete it here.
setup.agents.deleteUserNote: It's your own agent, outside this workspace, so History can't bring it back.
setup.agents.deleteProjectNote: You can bring it back from History with Roll back.
setup.agents.deleteRoleNote: The setup plan will offer to install this task role again.
setup.agents.intro: Agents Claude can hand work to, and profiles to run a chat or a Team worker as. Auto ones say “use proactively”, so Claude may start them on its own when a task fits; manual ones run when you or a prompt ask for them. When the app runs one, only the tools it lists are there. Changes apply to sessions started afterwards.
setup.agents.projectHelp: Each change is a run in History, so it can be rolled back.
setup.agents.userHelp: Your own agents. They're outside this workspace, so History doesn't cover them: a change is saved in place.
setup.agents.noUserAgents: None yet. To add one, pick “All my projects” in a new agent's form.
setup.agents.unreadable: {{file}} can't be read as an agent:
setup.agents.startFromHelp: A shipped task role or a starter fills in the form; nothing is saved yet.
setup.agents.name: Name
setup.agents.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is also the file name, in {{dir}}
setup.agents.descriptionHelp: When Claude should use it. Claude reads this to pick an agent.
setup.agents.autoCheck: Auto: Claude may start it on its own
setup.agents.mcpToolsHelp: Comma-separated: mcp__server for all its tools, or mcp__server__tool. Without any, the agent gets no MCP tools when the app runs it.
setup.agents.limitedHelp: When the app runs this agent (a chat or a Team worker), only these tools are there, still with approvals.
setup.agents.allToolsHelp: Every tool the session has. Approvals and the guard still apply.
setup.agents.toolsRequired: Tools: pick at least one, or allow all tools.
setup.deploys.intro: Production deploys of the workspace's current branch, with the provider's own CLI. Previews are made from a task's page.
setup.deploys.noConfig: No deploy config found. Vercel needs .vercel/project.json (vercel link); Cloudflare Workers need wrangler.toml, wrangler.json or wrangler.jsonc; Firebase Hosting needs firebase.json with a default project; Fly.io needs fly.toml; a Docker image needs a Dockerfile.
setup.deploys.noDeploys: No deploys yet. Each one is recorded here with its smoke test.
setup.deploys.imageHelp: With its registry and no tag, e.g. ghcr.io/you/app. Saved in .agentchainer/docker.json, which you can commit. Sign in with docker login.
setup.deploys.dockerRollbackDescription: The latest tag goes back to the previous commit's image in the registry, without a build.
setup.deploys.dockerDeployDescription: This builds the workspace's Dockerfile and pushes the image with the commit's tag and latest.
setup.deploys.rollbackDescription: Production goes back to the deploy before this one, with the provider's own rollback. The smoke test runs again.
setup.deploys.deployDescription: This deploys the workspace as it is now to the provider's production. The smoke test runs on the result.
setup.deploys.previousUnrecorded: The provider's previous production deploy (the app has no record of it).

setup.metrics.focusRetried: Tasks with retries or fix rounds

setup.plan.generating: Claude is reading the project and proposing files…
setup.plan.generateTitle: Claude reads the project (read-only) and proposes files; costs a model call

setup.plan.installFirst: Install dependencies first, so the tests can run: {{command}}
setup.plan.installFirstHelp: Downloads packages and may run their install scripts. Lockfile changes roll back with the run; installed packages stay.
setup.bootstrap.applyBody: Files are backed up first and the run is recorded in {{file}}. You can roll the run back from History.
setup.bootstrap.forceBody: Files you edited after the run are overwritten with their contents from before it.
setup.bootstrap.rollbackActionBody: Undoes what the action installed and restores the files it changed, byte for byte. Files you edited since are left alone.
setup.bootstrap.rollbackRunBody: Undoes what the run installed and restores the files it changed, byte for byte. Files you edited since are left alone.

setup.permissions.workspaceNote: Kept out of git, so only you have these.
setup.permissions.teamNote: Committed with the project, so everyone who opens it gets these.
setup.permissions.removeBody: {{rule}} is removed from {{file}}. Claude will ask again for it, certainly in new sessions.
setup.permissions.teamWarning: This file is committed: once you commit the change, it applies to your whole team.
setup.permissions.intro: Choosing Always allow on an approval saves a rule here, for you only or for your team. Session-only rules end with the session and aren't listed.
setup.workflows.intro: The steps a task runs, by tier. A project can replace a tier's with its own {{file}}, shared through git; it's checked like the app's own, and a run keeps a copy of the one it started with.
setup.summary.smallPrint: Review the readiness report, the bootstrap plan with exact previews, detected commands and past runs.
setup.history.empty: Nothing applied yet. Each apply is recorded here and can be rolled back.
setup.overview.eachHasFix: Each one has a fix in the plan.
setup.overview.nothingNeeded: Nothing in the readiness checks needs attention.
setup.workflows.defaultsHelp: How this workspace's tasks run unless a task chooses. Each field follows the app's default (Settings) until you set it here. Saved on change, out of git.
setup.workflows.applyAllBody: This workspace's own task defaults replace those of the {{count}} other workspaces the app knows (recent and named ones). A field this workspace leaves to the app's default is left to it there too.
setup.workflows.appliedSome: Applied to {{count}} workspaces; couldn't write to {{failed}}.
